A new cohort that reaffirms the programme’s mission: to nurture entrepreneurial talent across France Launched by Mission French Tech in 2019, French Tech Tremplin supports entrepreneurs from backgrounds, regions or social circumstances that remain under-represented in the innovation ecosystem.

This new cohort once again illustrates the wealth of talent across the whole of France and reaffirms the programme’s ambition: to foster the future success stories of French Tech by giving opportunities to entrepreneurs who, without this scheme, would find it more difficult to access support networks, funding and entrepreneurial resources.
The laureates are spread across all French regions, both in mainland France and in the overseas territories.

The 102 laureates will now receive support from partner incubators to consolidate their entrepreneurial projects, develop their businesses and join the French Tech community.

French Tech 2030
This third cohort is organized around 8 strategic sectors: artificial intelligence, space, quantum technology, cybersecurity, robotics, electronics, healthcare, energy and decarbonization.
Each sector addresses a strategic challenge – that is, a technology that France must master in order to shape its future.

Entalpic helps its industrial partners to accelerate the screening and discovery of materials used in atomic deposition and etching processes – which are essential for the development of new technologies – through a proprietary AI platform combining generative and predictive models, atomistic simulations and experimental data.
NPco is developing AI capable of simulating the physical behaviour of complex industrial systems in a matter of seconds, where traditional methods require days or even weeks of computation.
This technology is aimed at strategic and complex industries (aerospace, defence, energy, automotive, data centres, etc.) to accelerate design and reduce simulation costs.

Orasio develops AI solutions that detect sensitive situations in video streams, both in real time and retrospectively, for internal security forces, local authorities, critical infrastructure and the defence sector.
Outsight , through its physical AI, continuously digitises the movements, behaviours and interactions of people, vehicles and robots on a large scale, generating real-time Spatial Intelligence.

PyannoteAI develops speech intelligence: its models identify who is speaking, when, and in what context within any audio recording, and provide organisations with the essential building block for understanding the speech signal needed to move from a prototype to a voice AI system that is actually deployed in production.

Reeverse Systems provides the first comprehensive technology and solution for characterising, optimising, tracking and reusing strategic materials—both in planning and in real time—across the design and manufacturing chains of building equipment manufacturers (industrial joinery and metal fabricators), as well as in the aerospace, shipbuilding, rail, maritime and machinery sectors.
ZML is an AI engineering laboratory designing the universal execution layer between models and hardware.

Its technology decouples models from the underlying hardware, running any open-source model on any type of chip (GPU, TPU, CPU) at maximum performance, ensuring zero vendor lock-in and zero loss of quality.
Space Cailabs develops and manufactures photonic solutions for the space, defence, industrial and telecommunications sectors.

NEWS - Published on Wednesday 8 November 2023 The criteria for the French Tech Next40/120 programme are changing! To mark the 10th anniversary of French Tech, Jean-Noël Barrot, Minister Delegate for the Digital Economy, announced that the criteria for the French Tech Next40/120 programme would be revised to take greater account of changes in the start-up ecosystem. What is French Tech
French Tech Next40/120 is the French Tech Mission programme which supports the 120 most successful French scale-ups with the potential to become international leaders.
These companies receive support linked to their development challenges for one year, promoting them in France and internationally.

Changes proposed by French Tech Finance Partners to meet a threefold objective The French Tech Finance Partners body was launched in January 2023 by Jean-Noël Barrot , Minister Delegate in charge of the Digital Economy, to work on three priority areas: the financing of start-ups in the regions; the financing of DeepTech; and the selection criteria for French Tech programmes.

The programme’s cross-cutting criteria Constant generic criteria: As has been the case since the programme was created, companies must have their head office in France and must not be listed on the stock exchange.

ACTUALITÉ - Publiée le Jeudi 18 juillet 2024 La Mission French Tech associe son programme French Tech Rise au Fundtruck de Maddyness ! Parité et diversité Avec ce partenariat stratégique, Maddyness et la Mission French
French Tech Rise, lancé en 2021, vise à réduire les inégalités d’accès au financement des start-up des territoires et à valoriser le dynamisme des écosystèmes French Tech partout en France.

Déployé grâce au soutien de notre réseau de Capitales et Communautés French Tech, le programme permet à toutes les startups de l’écosystème French Tech de rencontrer des fonds de capital-risque nationaux à travers des événements et des rendez-vous réguliers : 70 en 2023, qui ont réunis près de 700 start-up et plus de 450 investisseurs dans toute la France.
Cette année, le Fundtruck sillonne les routes de France pour aller à la rencontre des entrepreneurs dans les 17 Capitales French Tech.
Les lauréats des différentes régionales seront invités à participer à la grande finale nationale qui aura lieu en fin d’année, à Paris.

Le French Tech Next40/120 est le programme de la Mission French Tech qui accompagne les 120 scale-up françaises les plus performantes et en capacité de devenir des leaders au niveau international .
Ces entreprises bénéficient d’un accompagnement lié à leurs enjeux de développement pendant un an, les valorisant en France et à l’international.

Des évolutions proposées par le French Tech Finance Partners, répondant à un triple objectif L’instance French Tech Finance Partners , a été lancée en janvier 2023 par Jean-Noël Barrot , ministre délégué chargé du Numérique, pour trois chantiers prioritaires : le financement des start-up en région ; le financement de la DeepTech ; et les critères de sélection des programmes French Tech.
